name: Discrete-Continuous Transition Mechanics Law
purpose: Define how continuous admissibility/reinforcement gradients may produce discrete continuation outcomes under threshold crossing.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Continuous changes in admissibility or reinforcement can generate discrete events when they cross operational thresholds that force selection, stabilization, pruning, fracture, or regime transition.

formal.continuous_state_candidate: G_A(U) := continuous admissibility/reinforcement gradient over region U
formal.discrete_event_candidate: E_D := event selected from {stabilize, prune, bifurcate, collapse, merge, redirect, regime_shift}
formal.threshold_crossing_condition: E_D occurs when G_A(U) crosses Θ_D(U) under declared admissibility, reinforcement, perturbation, or budget tolerance.
formal.stabilization_quantization: Q_stab(U) := partition of continuation outcomes induced by threshold-crossed admissibility regions
formal.continuity_preservation: Continuous pre-threshold variation is preserved as gradient structure even when post-threshold outcomes are discrete.
formal.nonphysical_discreteness: Discrete events are operational stabilization outcomes, not claims of physical quantization or quantum discreteness.
